title: Zellij corrupts escape sequences when keys repeat quickly.
body:
**Basic information**

`zellij --version`: zellij 0.42.2. Also tested 0.39 - 0.43.1: all exhibit.

`stty size`: 75 167

`uname -av` or `ver`(Windows): Linux ar12 6.1.0-18-amd64 #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Debian 6.1.76-1 (2024-02-01) x86_64 GNU/Linux



**The problem**

Context: Start a terminal app (I use Foot, but Kitty exhibits the same problem): ssh to server, run zellij there, open neovim.

In neovim, you can scroll with Ctrl-e and Ctrl-y. Without using zellij, if I hold down Ctrl-e it scrolls all through the document until the end. But when using zellij and doing the same, after a little scrolling vi seems to be fed something else, something that is the equivalent of pressing _undo_ a lot. This is observed by the vim message _"Already at oldest change"_.

This means that using zellij, which I've done for years (thank you!), I now can't scroll in vim - because if I do, I risk losing my work; it will un-do everything. Of course if I notice then I can do something like `1000<c-r>` to re-do, but if I don't notice, and start a new edit, everything previously is lost.

I _think_ this has gotten worse with the latest update, but I've retested and found it exhibits from 0.39 too. 

I do have repeat-keys set reasonably fast. 

## Edit: more info

While doing some investigation on this I found that doing this:

- start zellij with 2 panes (specifically: over an ssh connection in a terminal on gnome)
- full screen one pane
- run `cat >~/out`
- hold `<Ctrl-E>` down so it repeats lots.
- at some point, zellij drops full screen; goes back to the 2 panes.

This behaviour does not exhibit in `tmux`, so I think it's a zellij thing.




[zellij-23.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22662052/zellij-23.log)
[zellij.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22662053/zellij.log)

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Hey - thanks for the report and my apologies for the experience. If I had to wager a guess, I'd say this is https://github.com/wezterm/wezterm/issues/7076 - which is to say, problematic fragmentation over SSH. I'm hoping to be able to get a fix upstream, and if not I'll likely spend some time bypassing this or implementing our own STDIN parsing.

That being said, until this is fixed, as a workaround this will probably not happen in a terminal that supports the kitty keyboard protocol. My personal recommendation is Alacritty. You can also of course use the Zellij web server and connect through the browser - there this will almost definitely not happen (I use it as my daily driver and I code heavily in the terminal).

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Hey @reporter - I have at this point done every possible thing I can think of to reproduce this problem and was not able to.

I even reached a point where I'm running Zellij behind `socat` to allow me to inject chunks over STDIN at various sizes and intervals. I spammed it with 50k `Ctrl e` keypresses, both with KKP and without and got nothing with various chunk sizes.

While I'm not by any means discounting your experience, can you maybe do a bit of troubleshooting on your side? Find out if by any chance you have some special configuration in your setup that can explain this? Try from different machines, both as hosts (ssh to) and as clients (ssh from), try running the terminal emulators without any special configuration, etc. I honestly don't know what more to suggest. :)

I'll keep looking at different possibilities.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
@participant1 I think I managed to reproduce this locally on a Debian VM

In Alacritty run:

```
sudo modprobe sch_netem
# simulate packet delay on loopback
sudo tc qdisc add dev lo root netem delay 100ms 20ms distribution normal
ssh localhost
zellij
```

Then write a long line, go to its beginning and hold Ctrl-d.
